newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips rebound, tech shares depress Nasdaq.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips rebound, tech shares depress Nasdaq.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rebounded sharply on Tuesday from the previous day's losses, but the over-the-counter market remained depressed by concerns about the technology sector.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 36.49 points at 7,325.89, after hitting a session low of 7,254 and then jumping by more than 50 points.
The sharp rebound prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set trading curbs shortly after midday.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced declines by 14 to nine on volume of 297 million shares.

Among big-capitalisation stocks, financial, oil and drug stocks were mildly stronger, and consumer products company Procter & Gamble Co. recovered from a rating downgrade on Monday by Smith Barney, analysts said.

"There is a snap-back in big cap stocks," Legg Mason Wood Walker chief market strategist Richard Cripps said. "It's obvious that there is money out there that still wants to go into stocks and investors fear not participating in a market rise."
Smaller and middle-capitilization shares also continued to perform well, analysts said.

"The Dow is benefiting from a nice even distribution of buying," said Charles Payne, an analyst at Wall Street Strategist. "There is a flight to quality. Investors are trying to position themselves in good long-term places, in case the market gets rocky."
Blue-chip stocks drew support from a stronger bond market. The 30-year Treasury bond rose 6/32, reducing its yield to 6.89 percent from 6.90 percent at Monday's close.

But the Nasdaq index, laden with technology shares, fell 12.12 points to 1,392.67. The index was dragged down by losses in networking and disk drive makers, as well as Intel Corp., the leading maker of computer chips.
Intel was off four at 145-3/4, still weak after warning on Friday of disappointing second-quarter earnings due to weaker demand, especially in Europe.
"Intel is still under pressure and that has dampened enthusiasm for techs," one trader said.
Shares of technology firms took a hit following news from both Seagate Technology Inc. and Cabletron Systems Inc. that their quarterly earnings would be below forecast.
Seagate was off 3-1/2 at 38-7/8, while Cabletron fell 15-1/8 to 30-5/8. A sell-off in Cabletron shares triggered declines in other networking stocks.
Bay Networks Inc. slid 2-1/8 to 22-1/4, Cisco Systems Inc. was off 2-9/16 at 65-1/4 and 3Coms Corp. fell 3-7/16 to 45-5/8.
But smaller and middle-capitalisation shares continued to perform reasonably well, analysts said.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks was up 2.65 points at 849.01. The Russell 2000 index of smaller capitalisation issues was barely changed, off 0.05 point at 383.47.
